summary: Explains serial for updating a few hosts at a time and shows pre_tasks that disable Nagios alerts and remove the web server from HAProxy via delegate_to loops. Notes each serial batch acts as a full play, so a fully failed batch fails the run.
questions: How do I update web servers one at a time in Ansible?
What does the serial keyword do?
How do I take a server out of the load balancer before updating it?
What happens if all hosts in a serial batch fail?

answer_card.title: Rolling updates with serial and pre_tasks
answer_card.answer_md:
```yaml
- hosts: webservers
  serial: 1        # e.g. 10 for 100 hosts
  pre_tasks:
  - nagios:
      action: disable_alerts
      host: "{{ inventory_hostname }}"
      services: webserver
    delegate_to: "{{ item }}"
    loop: "{{ groups.monitoring }}"
  - shell: echo "disable server myapplb/{{ inventory_hostname }}" | socat stdio /var/lib/haproxy/stats
    delegate_to: "{{ item }}"
    loop: "{{ groups.lbservers }}"
```

Without `serial`, Ansible parallelizes up to `forks`. Each serial batch is a full play: if every host in a batch fails, the whole run fails (consider this with `max_fail_percentage`). `pre_tasks` run before roles.
